testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is a dual air brake system?

options.text: A single air brake system that uses two sets of controls.
One air brake system for each side of the truck.
Two separate air brake systems that use one set of controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two separate air brake systems that use one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. They share one set of controls. One system usually controls the brakes on the rear axle. The other system controls the brakes on the front axle.

questions.question: What does the air compressor do in a truck's air brake system?

options.text: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
Moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks. The air compressor governor controls how much air goes into the tanks.

questions.question: What is the purpose of air tank drains?

options.text: They allow rain water to enter the tanks.
They remove water and oil from the tanks.
They must stay open while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They remove water and oil from the tanks.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. If water and oil build up in the system, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: When inspecting brakes, how much should a slack adjuster move from where it connects to the push rod?
questions.correctAnswerText: No more than one inch
questions.explanation: Check each slack adjuster by pulling on it. It should not move more than one inch from where it connects to the push rod. If it moves more than one inch, the adjuster is out of adjustment and needs to be fixed.

questions.question: What type of air brake system do most heavy-duty vehicles use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dual air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. These have two separate braking systems that share one set of controls. Each system controls the brakes on different axles.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, what is the maximum air leak for a single vehicle with air brakes in one minute?
questions.correctAnswerText: 2 psi
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should leak no more than 2 psi per minute. If it leaks faster, do not drive the vehicle. Something needs to be repaired.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, if one system leaks, what happens?

options.text: The other system may not be affected.
The other system will also leak.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other system may not be affected.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. If one system leaks, the other system may still work properly.

questions.question: When should you test the low pressure warning signal?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every trip.
questions.explanation: Test the low pressure warning light before each trip. After the system builds up pressure, rapidly press and release the brake pedal to release air. The warning signal should turn on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual brake system, what should a driver do?

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up so fuel reaches the engine.
Wait for air pressure to build in both brake systems.
Start driving right after the engine starts.
Pump the pedal 20 times to build pressure, then drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for air pressure to build in both brake systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving, allow time for the compressor to build up air pressure to at least 100 psi in both systems.

questions.question: What is true about the parts in a dual air brake system?

options.text: Each system has its own separate air tanks, hoses, and lines.
The systems share air tanks, but have separate hoses and lines.
Each system uses the same lines and hoses.
One system is main, and a second is a backup.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own separate air tanks, hoses, and lines.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share one set of controls, but each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: If the ABS warning light comes on while driving, what does it mean?

options.text: The ABS has just been activated.
The ABS is not working properly.
The ABS needs to be activated.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow warning lights. If the light comes on, something is wrong with the braking system. You may have lost ABS on one or more wheels.

questions.question: What should you do when driving down a steep hill?

options.text: Shift into a lower gear, then use brakes to slow down.
Downshift instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into a lower gear, then use brakes to slow down.
questions.explanation: On a downgrade, let the engine do most of the braking work. Shift to a lower gear before going down the hill. Use the brakes only when you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the brake pedal.
Be careful because the brakes may fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not press the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using both at the same time can damage the brakes.

questions.question: If your tractor has ABS but your trailer does not, what happens?

options.text: The ABS will still help you steer better.
The ABS will make jackknifing easier.
The ABS will help others see when you brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS will still help you steer better.
questions.explanation: Even if only the tractor has ABS, it will improve your steering control. Watch the trailer and ease off the brakes if it starts to swing.

questions.question: What is the most common type of foundation brake?
questions.correctAnswerText: S-cam drum brake.
questions.explanation: The S-cam drum brake is the most common type of foundation brake.

questions.question: For a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, what is the maximum air leakage rate during a static leakage test?
questions.correctAnswerText: 5 psi per minute
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle with air brakes should not lose more than 5 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster than this, do not drive the vehicle. Something needs to be repaired.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure in an air brake system gets too low?

options.text: The brakes will be very sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may not work.
questions.explanation: If you use the brake pedal too much, air runs out faster than the compressor can replace it. If air pressure gets too low, the brakes will stop working.

questions.question: When should the low air pressure warning signal turn on?
questions.correctAnswerText: When pressure drops below 60 psi.
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning must turn on if tank pressure falls below 60 psi. The warning can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: When should you not use the parking brake?

options.text: When the brakes are very hot.
When the brakes are very cold.
When there is snow on the ground.
When there is water on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the brakes are very hot.
questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake if the brakes are very hot from driving down a steep hill. Heat can damage the brakes. Also, do not use it if brakes are wet in freezing weather because they may ice up.

questions.question: What does the emergency brake system use?

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system.
Only parts of the service brake system.
Parts from both the parking and service brake systems.
Only parts unique to the emergency brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts from both the parking and service brake systems.
questions.explanation: An air brake system has three separate brake systems: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: A vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) uses a ____ light to warn that the system is not working.
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: ABS warning lights are usually yellow. If the ABS is not working, you can still use your regular brakes.

questions.question: A tank endorsement is:

options.text: Required to transport both liquids and gases.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required to transport both liquids and gases.
questions.explanation: A tank endorsement is required to drive a tank vehicle that carries liquids or gases.

questions.question: The ____ shows how much air pressure is in the air tanks.
questions.correctAnswerText: Supply pressure gauge
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge tells the driver how much air pressure is in the air tanks.

questions.question: At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag can add ____ to your total stopping distance.
questions.correctAnswerText: 32 feet
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: When spring brakes activate in an air brake vehicle, you should never:
questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brake pedal down.
questions.explanation: Never push the brake pedal when spring brakes are activated. Using both at the same time can damage the brakes.
